item.title: Structural Results on the Unfair 0-1 Polynomial Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.14596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A $0$-$1$ polynomial is a polynomial whose coefficients are all either $0$ or $1$. The unfair $0$-$1$ polynomial conjecture states that if $f$ is a $0$-$1$ polynomial and $f(x)=g(x)h(x)$ is a factorisation into non-constant polynomials with non-negative real coefficients, then $g$ and $h$ must themselves be $0$-$1$ polynomials. We call $f$ fair if every such factorisation has this property, and unfair otherwise. In this paper, we study structural properties of possible unfair factorisations and obtain conditions which guarantee fairness. In particular, we prove that if $$ f(x)=x^{n-\operatorname{deg} w}w(x)+v(x), $$ where $v$ and $w$ are $0$-$1$ polynomials and $v$ is fair, then $f$ is fair whenever $$ n\geq\max\{\operatorname{deg} w+2\operatorname{deg} v,\,2\operatorname{deg} w\}. $$
item.dc:creator: Emina Hasanbegovi\'c

item.title: Universal Invariants for $\gcd(n^k-1,n!-1)>1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.14600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For integers $k\geq2$ and $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\in\{-1,+1\}$, let $S_k^{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}:=\{n\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\{0,1\}:\gcd(n^k+\lambda_1,n!+\lambda_2)>1\}$. This family arose from a MathOverflow problem concerning the existence of integers $n$ satisfying $\gcd(n^2+1,n!+1)>1$ and from the subsequent question of whether arbitrarily many, but finitely many, solutions can be obtained by varying the exponent and the signs. We concentrate on the case $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=-1$ and introduce the notion of a universal invariant for an odd prime $p$, namely an integer $n\geq2$ such that $\gcd(n^{p\cdot m}-1,n!-1)>1$ for every integer $m\geq1$. We prove that this condition is equivalent to $\gcd(n^p-1,n!-1)>1$, characterize the possible prime divisors in terms of roots of unity over finite fields, and recall an explicit construction due to Jonathan Love that yields a universal invariant for every odd prime $p\geq5$, with the cubic case treated separately. As an application, we prove that $|S_k^{-1,-1}|\geq\omega_{\mathrm{odd}}(k)$ for every integer $k\geq2$, where $\omega_{\mathrm{odd}}(k)$ denotes the number of distinct odd prime divisors of $k$. Hence, the cardinalities of these sets are unbounded as $k$ varies. This lower bound is deliberately coarse and constructive, as it is obtained by considering only universal invariants; stronger general lower bounds are obtained by different constructions. We also discuss minimal universal invariants, their persistent common divisors, the special structure of the cubic case, and a heuristic due to Will Sawin suggesting that there may be infinitely many cubic universal invariants, although the known examples are exceptionally sparse. Whether $S_k^{-1,-1}$ is finite or infinite for any fixed exponent $k\geq3$ remains an open problem.
item.dc:creator: Marco Rip\`a

item.title: A Master Identity for Forsyth-Glaisher-Type Series for $1/\pi$
item.description: arXiv:2611.14874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive a novel three-parameter master identity for Forsyth-Glaisher-type series for $1/\pi$. By unifying disparate results from the literature into a single overarching framework, we demonstrate that Glaisher's original series and numerous known variations emerge naturally as special cases through systematic choices of the parameters. This master identity simplifies the derivation of existing formulas, provides a mechanism for generating an infinite number of new series for $1/\pi$, and is further utilized to derive associated series involving harmonic and odd harmonic numbers.
item.dc:creator: Kunle Adegoke

item.title: Meta-Nested Recurrences
item.description: arXiv:2611.15815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study recurrences in which a previous sequence value determines the number of iterations of an inner map. Campbell's example has an explicit power-of-three formula and inner orbits of eventual period at most two. Its normalized lower and upper limits are $2/5$ and $3/4$. For a variable-depth Conway recurrence $C$, we prove the golden-ratio lower bound, its exact equality set, a Fibonacci upper cap, and the landing of the inner orbit at every Fibonacci index $F_k$ with $k\ge6$. These proofs are elementary and start from twenty-four initial values. The plateau of $C$ to the left of $F_k$ has width exactly $\lfloor(2k-9)/3\rfloor$, and $C(F_k+t)=F_{k-1}+t$ for $0\le t\le\lfloor(k-8)/6\rfloor$. A maximum principle turns a finite exact computation into the bound $\limsup C(n)/n<0.65446923$. We characterize the convergence of $C(n)/n$ to $\alpha=(\sqrt5-1)/2$ in terms of negative selected orbit jumps and of a limiting convex profile, and we derive entropy and variance budgets for the recursive splits. Along inverse rays of the map $x\mapsto C(x)$, the relative errors are absolutely summable and the growth is asymptotically Fibonacci. For Grytczuk's fixed-depth recurrence, we give a Pascal-word proof of convergence with the sharp error order $n/\sqrt{\log n}$ along interval maxima. The full variable-depth limit remains open.
item.dc:creator: Beno\^it Cloitre, Haobo Ma, Wenlin Zhang

item.title: Characterizations of Pettis Integrable Multifunctions in Locally Convex Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.16969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present characterizations of Pettis integrability in $bcc(X)$ and $cwk(X)$ of a multifunction $\Gamma : \Omega \to cc(X)$, where $(\Omega, \Sigma, \mu)$ is a complete finite measure space and $cc(X)$ $(bcc(X), cwk(X))$ is the family of all nonempty convex closed (bounded convex closed, convex weakly compact) subsets of a Hausdorff locally convex topological vector space $X$. Incidentally, a convergence theorem for scalarly integrable multifunctions is proved. As an application, we are going to prove full characterizations of Pettis integrability for fuzzy maps defined on $\Omega$ and taking values in the generalized fuzzy number hyperspace $\mathcal{F}_{cwk}(X)$.
item.dc:creator: Sokol Kaliaj

item.title: Duality in Biperiodic Fibonacci Words: Substitution, Frequencies and Combinatorial Invariants
item.description: arXiv:2607.16844v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The biperiodic Fibonacci word $\mathfrak{F}^{(a,b)}$ is the standard Sturmian word with directive sequence $(a,b,a,b,\dots)$. The words $\mathfrak{F}^{(a,b)}$ and $\mathfrak{F}^{(b,a)}$ are related by the morphism $\sigma_a\colon 0\mapsto 0^a1,\ 1\mapsto 0$ through the exact identity $\mathfrak{F}^{(a,b)}=\sigma_a\bigl(\mathfrak{F}^{(b,a)}\bigr)$. This identity gives the letter frequencies, the return words of both letters, the derived sequence with respect to the letter $0$, and the transport of palindromic prefixes from $\mathfrak{F}^{(b,a)}$ to $\mathfrak{F}^{(a,b)}$. The slope of $\mathfrak{F}^{(a,b)}$ has the continued fraction expansion $[0;a+1,\overline{b,a}]$, and the critical exponent equals $2+\alpha/\min(a,b)$, where $\alpha$ is the positive root of $t^2-ab\,t-ab=0$. The frequency of the letter $1$ and the return words of $1$ depend on the order of $a$ and $b$, whereas the critical exponent, the balance, the abelian complexity and the palindromic complexity do not.
item.dc:creator: Jasem Hamoud
